# HarnessDock v0.2.4

v0.2.4 makes the Harness Web UI the mandatory desktop startup surface and turns Shell Settings into a true on-demand plugin window.

## Web-first startup

- Desktop startup keeps the main control surface hidden and always opens the official Harness Web UI after Runtime readiness.
- Added retry logic around window creation/navigation so transient WebView timing failures do not leave the user on the control page.
- Third-party plugin failures remain isolated through recovery/quarantine and temporary safe-profile startup; the Web UI remains the usable destination whenever Runtime can provide a loopback address.

## Runtime resilience

- If a compatible system Node is present, HarnessDock still reuses it without installing anything system-wide.
- If system Node fails to boot the pinned Runtime, HarnessDock automatically retries with the bundled portable Node.
- Existing Windows path normalization and console-free child process behavior are retained.

## Shell Settings plugin

- Added a separate local `settings` WebView window, created only after the top Harness toolbar button or native HarnessDock menu is clicked.
- Settings can inspect Runtime/Node/recovery state, reopen Harness Web, restart Runtime, clear plugin quarantine and stop Runtime.
- Added a dedicated capability boundary: the Harness Web shell can only request the settings window; the settings window receives only its own recovery commands.
- Settings never competes with the Harness Web first screen and closing it does not stop the Runtime.

## Verification

- Release is gated by the same-SHA green CI and full Tauri candidate matrix.
